# Resource Leveling

Resolving over-allocation by moving tasks in time rather than by adding capacity. A schedule built
from dependencies alone assumes infinite parallelism; the moment finite people are assigned to it,
tasks that used to overlap must be pushed apart. Leveling is the act of doing that, and its price
is always duration.

In [[computer-project-management]] the price is stated exactly:

> "The extra 11 days come from **resolving over-allocation**: once a resource can only do one"
> — Computer Project Management/lab3-4_Resource_Assignment/README.md, 2026-07-10

| | Lab 2 — dependencies only | Lab 3–4 — resourced and leveled |
|---|:--:|:--:|
| Tasks | 38 | 38 |
| Duration | 110 d | **121 d** |
| Finish | 5 Aug 2026 | **20 Aug 2026** |

Same 38 tasks, same dependency network, +11 days. Nothing about the work changed — only the
assumption that people can be in two places at once.

## The two-step that makes it visible

The lab structure separates *defining* resources from *assigning* them, and that separation is what
makes the cost measurable. Lab 2 creates a 12-item pool — 9 work resources, 2 cost resources, 1
material resource — and assigns **none** of it. Lab 3–4 assigns all nine people, MS Project flags
the over-allocations, and leveling clears them. Had both happened in one step, the 11 days would
have been invisible inside a single number.

Assignments follow role bands rather than individuals: analysis and management, build (often paired
— *Design shipment tracking database* takes Backend Developer + Database Admin), quality and
release, handover, and two all-hands tasks.

## Leveling vs the alternatives

| Response to over-allocation | Effect | Taken here |
|---|---|---|
| **Level** — delay or sequence the conflicting tasks | duration grows, cost flat | yes, +11 d |
| **Smooth** — move only tasks with float, protect the finish date | duration flat, less slack | not distinguished from leveling anywhere in the repo |
| **Add a resource** | duration may shrink, cost grows | not taken — and the repo's own seminar argues against it via Brooks' Law, see [[project-environment-factors]] |
| **Overtime / raise availability** | duration flat, cost grows | not considered in any readable file |

Leveling appears twice in this plan under two different names: once here, and again in lab 5–6
where a Backend Developer conflict is resolved by re-linking two tasks — a manual leveling action
recorded as a dependency decision, [[sequence-integration-after-unit-testing]].
